main_text.p: les imagines. Ἐννοίας quidem inconspicuæ ima-go conspicua est Νοῦς, id est, Mens. Θελήσεως autem visibilis typus est Ἀλήθεια, id est, Veritas. Itaque & nominibus & modo ipso procreandi Æonas diuersus fuit a præceptore Valentino Ptolemæus. Sed iam in eo differunt Tertullia-nus & Irenæus, quòd Irenæus dicat Ptolemæum facere hos Æonas Bythi, id est, summi Dei Βυθοῦ tantum quasdam & Δυνάμεις, id est, affectus tantum & qualitates siue potestates. Tertullianus contrà scribit eum distinxisse Æonas in per-fonales substantias, & cesuisse esse res per se subsistentes, non tantum Dei affectus. Itaque uti Plato ideas suas ἰδέας esse dixit, sic iste Æonas suos, si Tertullianum sequimur. Ego tamen po-tius Irenæo assentior, quem etiam Epiphanius sequitur: & in eo Ptolemæus a Secundo condi-scipulo suo dissentire voluit, præceptorisque Valentini sententiam tueri, quam Secundus op-pugnarat.
2 Error. Legem veteris Testa-menti non totam à Deo esse dixit, sed partim à Deo, partim à Mose ipso: partim ex quibusdam seniorum traditionibus constare.

3 Deum u-num & eundem, cùm aliquid emittit Patrem uo-cari: cùm vera dicit, Veritatem: cùm se manife-stat, Hominem, vt Sabellianorum errorem spar-sisse, etsi obscurè, cū Simone videri debeat Pto-lemæus. Ita Irenæus lib.i.cap.6.

page.notes: Show-through from the reverse side of the leaf is visible at the foot of the page and was left out. Section numbers 2 and 3 open paragraphs and are kept in the text. The printed "Error." and "Deum" are set in a different type and are kept as printed. Words broken at line ends keep their printed hyphens. Greek is transcribed as printed; the Greek of the first line and of "Θελήσεως" was read with some uncertainty, though no word was marked [?].
